role.altitude: The research scientist keeps framing problems, judging results, inventing new uses and persuading managers and vendors; boilerplate code, first literature sweeps, status chasing and typing meeting notes shrink.
skills_to_grow: Reviewing generated code and tests as critically as a colleague's
Checking every cited paper before relying on it
role.ambitious_version: A researcher who tries three prototype designs in the time one used to take, and drops the weak ones sooner.

tasks.short: Analyze problems with stakeholders, review prior work, build prototypes and experiments to develop solutions involving computer hardware and software, evaluate results and write up the solution.

steps.what: Research scientist analyzes the problems with stakeholders
Research scientist reviews prior work and literature on the problem

loop.input: The defined problem and open paper and code repositories.
loop.output: A list of relevant papers and projects, each with a link and a quoted passage.
loop.check: The scientist opens every listed source before relying on it and checks that the quote says what the listing claims and bears on the problem; unlisted sources found by hand are added.
loop.stop: One sweep per problem, rerun when the problem changes.
loop.why_not_simpler: Keyword search misses work that uses other terms.

steps.what: Research scientist builds prototypes and experiments to develop solutions in hardware and software

loop.input: The scientist's description of a change and the prototype's repository.
loop.output: Code and tests in a branch.
loop.check: Tests and a security scan run on every change; the scientist reads every change and checks that it does what the experiment needs, not only that tests pass, before merging.
loop.stop: The scientist merges or discards the branch.
loop.why_not_simpler: Prototype code varies too much for templates.

steps.what: Research scientist evaluates results and decides the solution
Research scientist writes up the solution for the team

tasks.design: A search step over paper and code repositories lists prior work with links and quotes, and the scientist reads what matters. A coding assistant writes prototype code and tests in branches, and every change is tested, scanned and read before merging. Framing, evaluation and choice stay with the scientist. The write-up uses a team template.
tasks.previous_blocker: Prototype code and literature sweeps were written and done entirely by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Coding assistants that work in branches and search over paper repositories.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing which problem is worth solving.

reach.learn: Whether prototypes arrive with tests they can reuse.

evidence.claim: Field trials with 4,867 developers found 26% more completed tasks with an AI coding assistant.
In a randomised study, 16 experienced open-source developers were 19% slower with AI while feeling faster.
Models wrote vulnerable code in 45% of tests.
A coding assistant offers completion, review and a background coding agent, with oversight expected.

assumptions: Boundary: from problem to written solution; building the production system is outside.
The prototype's repository has a test pipeline and security scan set up by the team.
Framing and evaluation keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of research time spent coding.
research_questions: Do prototypes reach a decision sooner?

already_counted.description: Research scientist reads and corrects generated code.

incremental.description: Research scientist keeps the test pipeline and scan settings current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the code is unfamiliar, so reading and correcting generated code takes almost as long as writing it (s3 keeps 95), and the search lists many off-topic sources (s2 keeps 90) (4.2); high: prototype work in common languages as designed (11.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Identify a new use, apply theoretical expertise and innovation to create or apply new technology, survey related work, build a proof of concept, test it with users and write up the results.

steps.what: Research scientist identifies a new use and adapts principles for applying computers to it
Research scientist surveys related work and patents

loop.input: The framed idea and open paper and patent databases.
loop.output: A list of related papers and patents with links and quoted claims.
loop.check: The scientist opens every listed source and checks that the quote says what the listing claims and bears on the new use; patent questions go to the IP adviser.
loop.why_not_simpler: Keyword search misses work that uses other terms.

steps.what: Research scientist designs and builds the proof of concept to create or apply new technology

loop.input: The scientist's design and the proof-of-concept repository.
loop.output: Code and tests in a branch.
loop.check: Tests and a security scan run on every change; the scientist reads every change and checks that it does what the proof of concept needs, not only that tests pass, before merging.
loop.stop: The scientist merges or discards the branch.

steps.what: Research scientist tests the proof of concept with users
Research scientist writes up the results in the results template

tasks.design: The idea and the design stay with the scientist. A search step lists related papers and patents with quotes. A coding assistant writes proof-of-concept code and tests in branches that the scientist reads before merging. User tests and the write-up stay human, with a results template.
tasks.previous_blocker: Proofs of concept took weeks of hand-written code.
tasks.enabler_now: Coding assistants and search over paper and patent databases.
tasks.still_hard: Ideas whose value only shows after users try them.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing a use nobody has asked for yet.

ambition.what: Test more ideas per year with quick proofs of concept.

tasks.altitude: Quicker proofs of concept; invention stays human.

reach.learn: Whether more tested ideas improve choices.

evidence.claim: Autonomous coding agents raised commits 240% but releases 30% across 500,000+ developers.
Field trials with 4,867 developers found 26% more completed tasks.

assumptions: Boundary: from idea to tested proof of concept; productising is outside.
The repository has a test pipeline and security scan.
s5 keeps 85: the results template gives the headings and layout; the scientist still writes the results.
unknowns: How much proof-of-concept code is reused.
research_questions: Are more ideas tested per year?

already_counted.description: Research scientist reads and corrects generated code.

incremental.description: Research scientist checks related-work lists for missed sources.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: hardware-heavy concepts with little code, so s3 keeps 95, and the search lists many off-topic sources, so s2 keeps 90 (4.1); high: software concepts in common stacks as designed (9.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Set priorities and goals with the manager, assign or schedule tasks to team members, track progress and reschedule when priorities change.

steps.what: Research scientist sets work priorities and goals with the manager
Research scientist breaks work into tasks and assigns or schedules them for team members
Team members move their own tasks on the board and link code changes to them
Research scientist tracks progress from stand-ups, chats and mails
Research scientist reschedules tasks when priorities change

tasks.design: Tasks live on a project board. Team members move their own tasks, and code changes linked to a task update its status when merged, so the board shows progress without asking around. Setting priorities, breaking work into tasks, assigning and rescheduling stay with the scientist. The board shows tasks, not individual output.
tasks.previous_blocker: Progress was collected by asking in stand-ups and chats.
tasks.enabler_now: Project boards linked to code repositories.
tasks.still_hard: Research tasks whose length nobody can predict.

reach.learn: Whether the board answers their questions.

evidence.claim: Project dashboards can replace manual status collection.
Usage dashboards that can observe staff need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: planning and tracking the team's tasks; doing them is outside.
Input contract for s3: team members move their own tasks on the board and link code changes to tasks; about 75% of tasks are tracked this way; s3 is priced at that share.
Priorities, breaking work into tasks and rescheduling keep their full time. Team members' own task moves are shown in s5.
unknowns: How many people the scientist plans for.

incremental.description: Research scientist keeps the board tidy.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only half of tasks are kept current on the board, so the scientist still asks around and s3 keeps 80 (5.3); high: about 75% of tasks tracked on the board as assumed (11.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare and meet with managers, vendors and others to solicit cooperation and resolve problems, write notes and action points, check and send them, and follow up actions.

steps.what: Research scientist prepares the meeting: agenda, background and open actions
Research scientist meets with managers and vendors to solicit cooperation and resolve problems
Research scientist writes notes and action points

loop.input: The transcript of an online meeting recorded with all participants' consent.
loop.output: Draft notes with decisions and action points.
loop.check: The scientist checks each note and action point against what was said in the transcript, corrects the draft, and marks as open any decision that was not clearly agreed; an action owner is named only if the transcript shows they agreed.
loop.why_not_simpler: Decisions are spread through free conversation.

steps.what: Research scientist checks the final notes
Research scientist sends the approved notes to managers and vendors
Research scientist follows up open action points

approvals.approved_version: The meeting notes and action points exactly as checked by the scientist in s4, sent once to the meeting's participants; any change needs a new check.

tasks.design: The agenda template pulls open action points from the previous meeting. Meetings stay human. For online meetings recorded with everyone's consent, a summarising step drafts notes and action points, which the scientist corrects, checks and sends. Action points go on the project board with due dates and reminders.
tasks.previous_blocker: Notes were typed from memory after each meeting.
tasks.still_hard: Vendors who agree in the meeting and stall afterwards.
tasks.human_edge: Getting a reluctant manager or vendor to cooperate.

reach.learn: Whether written action points speed up fixes.

evidence.claim: Meeting tools transcribe online meetings and models draft notes from transcripts.
A service desk tool summarises tickets and drafts knowledge items for review.

assumptions: Boundary: one meeting from preparation to follow-up.
Input contract for s3: online meetings recorded with all participants' consent, about 60% of meetings; in-person meetings are noted by hand; s3 is priced at that share.
The meeting itself and sending keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of vendors who agree to recording.

incremental.description: Research scientist asks participants for consent to recording.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only about a third of meetings are recorded with consent, so s3 keeps 80 (6.7); high: about 60% of meetings recorded as assumed (9.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
